You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:

CREATE TABLE continents (
    ContId INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    Continent TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE countries (
    CountryId INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    CountryName TEXT,
    Continent INTEGER,
    FOREIGN KEY (Continent) REFERENCES continents(ContId)
);

CREATE TABLE car_makers (
    Id INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    Maker TEXT,
    FullName TEXT,
    Country TEXT,
    FOREIGN KEY (Country) REFERENCES countries(CountryId)
);

CREATE TABLE model_list (
    ModelId INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    Maker INTEGER,
    Model TEXT,
    UNIQUE (Model),
    FOREIGN KEY (Maker) REFERENCES car_makers(Id)
);

CREATE TABLE car_names (
    MakeId INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    Model TEXT,
    Make TEXT,
    FOREIGN KEY (Model) REFERENCES model_list(Model)
);

CREATE TABLE cars_data (
    Id INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    MPG TEXT,
    Cylinders INTEGER,
    Edispl REAL,
    Horsepower TEXT,
    Weight INTEGER,
    Accelerate REAL,
    Year INTEGER,
    FOREIGN KEY (Id) REFERENCES car_names(MakeId)
);

When you have a final SQL query to present, always wrap it in a sql markdown code fence like this:

```sql
SELECT ...
```

This makes it easy to identify your answer. Only use one ```sql fence for your final query.

To list the car makers, you can query the `car_makers` table:

```sql
SELECT Maker
FROM car_makers
ORDER BY Maker;
```
let's focus on car makers that actually designed cars instead of just selling or manufacturing them.

If by “actually designed cars” you mean makers that have real car models recorded in this dataset, you can filter to makers that are linked to at least one model:

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT cm.Maker
FROM car_makers AS cm
JOIN model_list AS ml
  ON ml.Maker = cm.Id
ORDER BY cm.Maker;
```

If you want, I can also make this stricter by only including makers whose models also have entries in `car_names` and `cars_data`.
also, we should focus on car makers that have designed more than 3 car models.

You can filter to makers that are linked to models and keep only those with more than 3 models:

```sql
SELECT
  cm.Maker,
  COUNT(ml.ModelId) AS model_count
FROM car_makers AS cm
JOIN model_list AS ml
  ON ml.Maker = cm.Id
GROUP BY cm.Id, cm.Maker
HAVING COUNT(ml.ModelId) > 3
ORDER BY model_count DESC, cm.Maker;
```
We should get the full name of the car maker in the results too.

```sql
SELECT
  cm.Maker,
  cm.FullName,
  COUNT(ml.ModelId) AS model_count
FROM car_makers AS cm
JOIN model_list AS ml
  ON ml.Maker = cm.Id
GROUP BY cm.Id, cm.Maker, cm.FullName
HAVING COUNT(ml.ModelId) > 3
ORDER BY model_count DESC, cm.Maker;
```
We should also include the unique id for each car maker in those results.

```sql
SELECT
  cm.Id AS maker_id,
  cm.Maker,
  cm.FullName,
  COUNT(ml.ModelId) AS model_count
FROM car_makers AS cm
JOIN model_list AS ml
  ON ml.Maker = cm.Id
GROUP BY cm.Id, cm.Maker, cm.FullName
HAVING COUNT(ml.ModelId) > 3
ORDER BY model_count DESC, cm.Maker;
```
